chunks: Al-ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a man praying in a woman’s garment or her waist-wrapper, and using her headcover as a turban. He عليه السلام said: “Yes, if she is trusted.”

key_terms.ثَوْبِ: a garment or item of clothing
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةً: trusted, especially regarding ritual purity and freedom from impurity

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to pray in a woman’s clothes or headcover?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about the permissibility of a man praying in garments belonging to a woman. The ruling permits it when the woman is maʾmūnah, meaning trusted with respect to ritual purity and the absence of najasah on the garment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man praying in a woman's garment or her waist wrap, or wrapping himself with her headcover.
Imam (as) said: "Yes, if it is clean (from any impurity)”.
